findings.description: This subnet is associated with an Internet Gateway default route and automatically assigns public IP addresses to launched instances. Workloads deployed here can become Internet-reachable when security-group rules permit it, weakening network segmentation.

This subnet is associated with an Internet Gateway default route and automatically assigns public IP addresses to launched instances. The portal_server is deployed in this subnet and has an Internet-reachable path when combined with its permissive security group.
The EBS volume does not explicitly enable encryption. In the absence of independently enforced account-level default EBS encryption, data written to this volume is stored unencrypted at rest.
User data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. These reusable credentials can be exposed through source control, Terraform state or deployment records, and instance user-data access.
TCP port 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0. The attached portal_server is in a public, Internet-routed subnet and is assigned a public IP, making SSH directly reachable from untrusted networks.
TCP port 80 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0. The attached portal_server is publicly reachable, exposing its HTTP service to all Internet sources without source-network restriction.
The bucket storing VPC flow logs has no explicit server-side encryption configuration. Sensitive network telemetry is therefore not protected by Terraform-enforced encryption at rest.
